details: Bitcoin continues to face downward pressure, trading near recent lows, as persistent inflation and rising expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes weigh on investor sentiment. Recent U.S. inflation data has fueled bets that the Fed will likely raise interest rates in December, which negatively impacts speculative assets like cryptocurrencies. Adding to the bearish outlook, U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) have experienced significant net outflows for three consecutive weeks, with over $239.9 million leaving these funds on November 17 alone, primarily from BlackRock's IBIT. This indicates a weakening institutional appetite and a broader "risk-off" environment across financial markets.
title: Global Macro Headwinds and Bitcoin Outflows Drive Bearish Sentiment

details: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and Swift are deepening their collaboration to explore using tokenized deposits for enhancing 24/7 cross-border payments. Major banks, including HSBC, Standard Chartered, and Bank of China Hong Kong, are participating in this initiative. The project aims to link Swift's blockchain-based ledger with Hong Kong's Project Ensemble settlement platform, facilitating real-time and programmable international transactions in multiple currencies. This effort aligns with global shifts towards modernizing payment systems using digital assets.
title: Hong Kong and Swift Advance Tokenized Deposit Pilot for 24/7 Global Payments

details: The World Bank Group (WBG) is investigating the use of regulated stablecoin infrastructure for its payment and financial settlement processes, partnering with Citi and Circle. The initiative aims to enhance the cost-efficiency, speed, and transparency of cross-border disbursements for WBG clients. Circle will provide its USDC stablecoin infrastructure for minting and settlement, while Citi will connect the system to its existing banking rails across over 180 jurisdictions. This exploratory phase will focus on an intermediated and interoperable payment model in borrower countries where digital assets are permitted.
title: World Bank Group Explores Stablecoin Payments with Citi and Circle

details: The Central Bank of Honduras (BCH) has entered into an academic and technical collaboration with Cosmos Labs and Peersyst Technology to research a potential central bank digital currency (CBDC), instant payments, and cross-border transfers. This initiative, documented in BCH's 2025 annual report, aims to evaluate how blockchain technology could strengthen the country's payment infrastructure, improve interoperability among financial institutions, and expand financial access for its citizens. The collaboration is currently exploratory and does not commit the central bank to implementing a digital currency.
title: Honduras Central Bank Partners to Research CBDC and Digital Payments
